questions.q: According to this lesson, in which of these places can PII enter an AI system, beyond a user directly typing it?
options: Only through direct user input — no other source matters
Retrieved context in a RAG system, accumulated conversation history, and even the model's own output can all carry PII
PII can never appear in a model's output, only in its input
PII only ever appears if a developer manually inserts it into the training data
questions.explain: The lesson lists direct input, RAG-retrieved documents, multi-turn conversation history, and model output as all being places PII can show up.

questions.q: What is the difference between a 'direct identifier' and a 'quasi-identifier,' as defined in this lesson?
options: They are two different names for the exact same concept
A direct identifier only applies to phone numbers; a quasi-identifier only applies to email addresses
A direct identifier has a recognizable fixed shape (like an email address); a quasi-identifier isn't sensitive alone but can identify someone when combined with other fields
Quasi-identifiers are always more sensitive than direct identifiers in every case
questions.explain: Direct identifiers like emails or SSNs have a catchable pattern, while quasi-identifiers like ZIP code, birth date, and job title only become identifying in combination.

questions.q: What does the redact() function example in this lesson actually do?
options: It permanently deletes the entire prompt if any PII is detected
It pattern-matches common direct identifiers like email, phone, and SSN and replaces each match with a labeled placeholder
It encrypts the entire conversation history using a private key
It automatically reports detected PII to a regulatory authority
questions.explain: The function iterates through regex patterns for direct identifiers and substitutes each match with a placeholder like [EMAIL].

questions.q: Why does this lesson say regex-based redaction reliably catches an email address but not 'my manager Sarah Chen in the Austin office'?
options: Regex cannot process any text containing the word 'manager'
An email address has a fixed, learnable shape that a pattern can match, while a name and location have no fixed pattern regex can rely on
Names and locations are never considered PII under any definition
Regex redaction is always slower than named entity recognition
questions.explain: Pattern matching depends on a learnable fixed structure, which direct identifiers have and names/locations generally don't.

questions.q: What does layering a Named Entity Recognition (NER) model on top of regex, as mentioned in this lesson, actually add?
options: It removes the need to ever redact direct identifiers like emails or SSNs
The ability to catch names, locations, and organizations that regex structurally can't match due to having no fixed pattern
It guarantees 100% detection of every possible quasi-identifier combination
It replaces the entire prompt with a single generic placeholder
questions.explain: NER is specifically useful for catching entities like names and locations that don't have the fixed shape regex depends on, complementing pattern matching rather than replacing it.
